standard_prerequisites.use: Unramified permanence under composition (Morphisms), the etale-at-a-point criterion for unramified dominant maps over unibranch bases (same chapter), and etale descent of the etale property (Descent); cited inputs with the four-step argument written in the retained span.

core_obligations: Shrink X to an open neighbourhood of x on which the composition g composed with f is etale.
Deduce that f is unramified from the unramified permanence lemmas.
Upgrade unramified to etale at x using integrality and geometric unibranchness via the dominant-unibranch lemma.
Conclude that g is etale at y by etale descent.

proof_roadmap.step: Shrink so the composition is etale and deduce f is unramified.
Upgrade to etale at x via the unibranch lemma and transfer to g by descent.

difficulty_reason: Given f : X -> Y and g : Y -> Z with g composed with f etale at x, Y integral and geometrically unibranch at y = f(x), and a specialization x' leading to x whose image is the generic point of Y, the lemma concludes both f is etale at x and g is etale at y. The proof is a written four-step argument: shrink X so the composition is etale, deduce f is unramified from the unramified permanence and etale-implies-unramified lemmas, upgrade to etale at x via the unibranch dominant lemma, and transfer etaleity to g by etale descent citing the syntomic-smooth-etale permanence lemma in Descent. Retained author proof at lines 10542-10553.
